results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 69 aligned units' outline summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph in spec order (p01-p69, with the verticals section p51-p52 after Six Axes and p46 before p45 in the register section, as the spec orders them). The five opening callouts are not spec paragraphs and are matched to null; they restate the thesis and supporting claims and add no off-spec idea.

results.draft_locus: Where the Marketplace Ends: Four Models ¶7
results.finding: The outliner marked only this unit as two ideas (transactional definition plus take rate on GMV). The spec's controlling idea for p15 joins the two deliberately (the rung is defined by money passing through the platform, and its revenue therefore becomes a take rate classifieds cannot observe), and every sentence serves that one idea, so it is one controlling idea. No other unit was marked.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: the scene and register to T1/T5, the four models, six axes and vertical table to T2 (and T1), the consequences section and verticals to T3, the patterns to T4, and trade-offs, failure modes, Chief Architect's view and questions to T5. The off-ladder software paragraphs (Four Models ¶11, Failure Modes ¶8) support T2/T5 by marking the boundary of the ladder and the neutrality decision it requires.

results.quote: while Adevinta's 2023 report shows the margin of its French business falling two points "mainly reflecting the evolution of the business mix with an increasing share of transaction services and a decreasing share of highly profitable advertising revenues".
results.finding: The paragraph ends on the Adevinta quotation with no sentence saying what the margin evidence shows; the spec's 'shows' (scope and seller mix change margins) is never stated, and the quote is about the endpoint (transaction services), not scope, so the contrast with the verticals' 70% margins is not like-for-like. Flow reader A (item 3) stopped here to work out what was being compared.

results.draft_locus: all other evidence, tables, figures and quotations
results.finding: Every other table (endpoint ladder, axes, verticals, consequences, register, trade-offs), Figures 1-4, the quotations (Meta, eBay, a16z, Gurley, OLX, DSA, Omnibus, Zillow, CarGurus, Adevinta 2019) and the statistics are introduced or followed by a sentence saying what they show (e.g. 'That is about 77% classifieds...', 'Read across the rows and Noor's proposal shrinks', 'The common thread is...').

results.quote: What to watch at group level: the share of contacts, leads and orders per profile;
results.finding: Declared conclusion_summary carrying 'the four decisions' and introducing 'the signals that show whether they hold'. The paragraph opens a new list with no reference to the four decisions and never says the signals show whether those decisions hold; its close ties the signals to endpoint changes instead. Unchanged since round 4.

All other transition_in entries are expressed at their boundary with the declared relationship and known information, e.g. 'The model is therefore an architecture decision' (cause_effect), 'Ingrid did not argue with the slide' (contrast), 'By the end of the afternoon' (time), 'Ingrid's first question, where does our job end' (elaboration), 'What each rung adds is what a marketplace takes on, or gives up' (elaboration), 'Veldmark's register and the documented moves bring every ... team back to one question' (cause_effect), 'The seven failures share a remedy' (problem_solution), 'It does not tell it whether the job is being done well' (contrast). The asks-section opener expresses the declared emphasis, though its wording is a flow problem (see flow_is_followable).

results.quote: First the vocabulary: after the grid that split Veldmark's four brands into twenty country-and-category rows, it defines four models
results.finding: Both readers describe the declared organising principle (vocabulary, consequences, judgement in prerequisite order) and place every section, but both had to re-read the roadmap: 'the grid' and its twenty rows are referred to as already seen, and the scene is folded into the vocabulary step. The intro reader was unsure for the same reason. Unchanged since round 4.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-B, section 3 item 1 ('I had to read it twice to see that "after the grid" means the scene section')

results.draft_locus: What Each Model Asks of the Architecture ¶1
results.quote: Of the axes in the vertical table, the endpoint reaches furthest into the systems
results.finding: Both readers stopped at this hinge: the axes were defined in the six-axes table, not the vertical table, and the sentence does not say plainly that the chapter returns from the verticals to the endpoint ladder. The spec's order is sound (one reader suggested a reorder, the other would move nothing); the wording obscures it. Unchanged since round 4.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-B, section 3 item 3 ('The bridge into the architecture section points to the wrong table')

results.draft_locus: Trade-offs: Where Should the Marketplace End? ¶3
results.quote: First, **I would treat every move down the ladder as a bet with an exit plan**.
results.finding: Reader B: after a third-person chapter with Ingrid as the actor, the first 'I' (and later 'A rule I use') made the reader stop to work out who was speaking, despite the signpost 'they are the author's, as a Chief Architect'. The first person is in the spec's controlling idea; the collision with the Group Chief Architect character remains.

results.draft_locus: What Each Model Asks of the Architecture ¶1 (table, Trust focus row)
results.quote: Valuation error, adverse selection, condition fraud
results.finding: 'Adverse selection' is a marketplace-economics term (the audience's does_not_know includes marketplace economics) used undefined in the consequences table and explained only later in Pattern 3 ('sellers whose homes are overvalued accept while the rest walk away (adverse selection)'). Unchanged since round 4.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-A, section 3 'Terms met before they were explained' ('adverse selection: appears in the "What Each Model Asks" table ... before Pattern 3 explains it')

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: One Group, Four Models ¶1
results.quote: earning about €75 million in buyer fees and shipping-label margin, a take rate of about 7%
results.finding: 'Take rate' is a marketplace-economics term the audience is declared not to know; it is used in the scene and defined only in the transactional section ('eBay defines take rate as "net revenues divided by GMV"'). The figures in the sentence let a reader guess it, which both readers said, but neither was given the term before its use. A short gloss at first use fixes it.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-B, section 3 'Terms met before they were explained' ('take rate: used in the scene ... and defined only in the transactional section')

results.finding: All other does_not_know terms are given at or before first use (GMV, VAS, PSP, KYB/KYC, DSA, DAC7, VIN, DMS, learning to rank, liquidity, iBuying, principal revenue, entitlements, true-ups, provisions, trader). 'Bounded contexts', 'event backbone' and 'read path' were flagged by flow readers as undefined, but they are standard architecture vocabulary for this audience of experienced architects (not on does_not_know); 'Adyen for Platforms' and 'inventory risk' were read correctly from context by both readers.

Opens with the declared puzzling scenario (five people, five answers), bridges to the claim that the model is an architecture decision, and gives a concrete roadmap. None of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report.
The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', introduces no new subtopic beyond the declared hand-off to liquidity, holds no body evidence, and does not end on a rephrased thesis alone.

It states what no single section states, that the five opening answers were each right for particular rows of the register, and says why it matters: recorded per country and category they become configuration, shared platforms are sized by the profiles that need them, and moves are reversed 'by changing a row rather than by a migration program'.

Returns to the five people's five answers, mapping each to rows of the register ('classifieds' for Tradeyard Portugal, 'becoming transactional' for three Safe Deal profiles, 'dealer subscriptions' for Motorvane, and so on), as the callback declares.

The intro reader predicted every expected section in order (Veldmark's grid, four models of the endpoint ladder, six axes and the profile, vertical comparison, what each model asks of the systems, documented moves, Veldmark's register, where the marketplace should end, failure modes, the Chief Architect's standing decisions and questions), the evidence (dated, documented public company records plus Veldmark as a constructed case) and the tone. Its uncertainty about where the grid comes from is the roadmap flow point recorded under flow_is_followable.

The cold reader named order, payment, payout, shipping, dispute and ledger contexts through a licensed PSP, deeper identity (KYC, DSA trader traceability), DAC7 reporting, buyer-protection liability, and the change in ranking's success label; and scoped it per category (goods, not cars or homes, citing leboncoin, Marktplaats and Kleinanzeigen), recorded as configuration in the profile register, as a bet with an exit plan. It did not cite OLX's pull-back as the reason for the exit plan, but the substance of the expected answer is present.
